BII)I SMOKING METHOD

F-l SAMPLING
Bid; sample shall be chosen at random from each bundle of bidis for this purpose. The bidis are generally packed in 10, 20 and 25 pieces. For tbis, 20 percent of bitlis (that is 2, 4, or 5 bid; pieces) shall be chosen for this test. From each lot of 500, select on random basis 100 bitlis. Weigh the selected bitlis and record their mass in mg. Then find out tbe average mass of 100 bitlis.Bidis witb mean mass z30 mg are selected for testing.

F-l LENGTH OF BIDI
After selecting the bidis on mass basis, measure their length in mm. The length of bidi varies from 55 to 90 10m. A~ bidi is hand rolled the variation up to 2 to 5 nun in length is noticed.

F-] CONOmONING OF THE SAMPLE
The bitlis selected on the basis of avenge mass (%30 mg) should be conditioned for 72 h at relative humidity (RH) of 60 � 2 percent and at a temperature 22~2�C before carrying out smoking test.

Tobacco and Tobacco Product Sectional Committee, FADC 4

FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standads, after the draft finalized by the Tobacco and Tobacco Product Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council.
Bidi is a common man's smoke. There being great variation in the different brands of bidis, it is necessary to lay down certain quality criteria, the broad objective of which will be to enable the consumers to get the standard product and to help in the promotion of the export of btdis.

This standard was first published in 1961. Subsequently, the first revision was issued in 1970 incorporating cylindrical bidis, tolerances on declared values of length and mass of 1 000 bidis 10 ensure uniformity in production and procedure for identification of Tendu and Ashltr! leaves. The requirements for arsenic and lead were deleted for they increase the cost of quality control without any proportionate utility. In the second revision issued in 1974, the proportion of wrapper was increased to 5S � 5 percent. Requirement for chloride content deleted. A more practical test for buring quality was prescribed in this revision. The third revision is being issued updating various requirements, bring the standard in line with the existing manufacturing and trade practices. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2: 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

IS 1'25 : 1992

Indian Standard BIDIS - S'PECIFICATION ( 1nird Revision)
1 SCOPE This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and tests for bidis manufactured in India from sun-cured country tobacco. This standard does not cover the requirements for flavour and aroma of bidts. 2 REFERENCES The Indian Standards listed below are necessary adjuncts to the standard: 3.4 Freedom from Mould Attack

Bidis shalt be free from mould attack, when examined by method prescribed in 6 of IS 5643 : 1989.
3.5 Freedom from Tobacco Beetle Attack The bidis shall be free from tobacco beetle attack when examined by the method prescribed in Annex C.

ANNEX A ( Clause 3.3 )
IDENTIFICATION OF TENDU AND ASHITRI LEAVES

A-I TENDU ( Dlospyrus sp, ) LEAVES Leaves are simple, up to 20 em long and 9 em wide; elliptical, with narrow base or if broad,
with a decurrence on the petiole. Young leaves are hairy, mature glaborous above, hairy beneath; coriaeeous nerve and reticulation raised above, secondary nerves impressed as broad furrows give the leaves wrinkled and thickened look.

A-2 ASHITRI ( Bauhinia sp.) LEAVES
Leaves are simple, short petioled, broader than longer, up to 10 em wide and 7�S cm Ions: mostly clefted, divided or little less than half way down into two rounded lobes; entire, obtuse, coriaceous, clothed more or less densely beneath with grey pubesence; base usually carbate, main nerves 7 to 9 with distinct pattern of reticulation.

IS 1925 : 1992

ANNEX B
( Clauses 3.2 and 3.3 )
DETERMINATION OF MASS OF TOBACCO AND WRAPPER LEAF

8-1 PROCEDURE
Take 100 bidis and keep at 27 � 2�C temperature and 65 � 2 percent relative humidity for 24 hours, then weigh them and record the mass. Then carefully open these bidis, one by one, and separate the tobacco contained in them from the wrapper leaf. Weigh separately

the tobacco and the wrapper leaves so obtained. Record their mass.
B-2 CALCULATION

Prom the mass so recorded estimate the mass of tobacco contained in 1 000 bidts and the percentage mass of the wrapper leaf.

ANNEX

C

( Clause 3.5 )
EXAMINATION FOR FREEDOM FROM TOBACCO BEETLE ATTACK

c-i PROCEDURE C-l.1 Take 5 bid;s and visually examine the surface or each for the presence of any penetration by the tobacco beetles. Cut open these bidis, one by one, on a clean white sheet of paper. C-l.2 Examine the material carefully for the

presence of tobacco beetle (Lasioderma serricorne) in all its stages, that is, larval, pupal and adult ( alive or dead), by naked eye (corrected for abnormal vision). A hand lens ( magnification 10 X) may also be used. In case a larger mangification is used, this fact may be stated in the test report.

ANNEX D
( Clause 3.8 )
TEST FOR BURNING QUALITY

1>-1 PROCEDURE
D-l.1 Light the bidl thoroughly by puffing for a few minutes. The bidi should burn continuously and evenly if puffed for 5 seconds at 50 second interval. The colour of the ash should not be black.

D-l.2 10 bidis shall be tested for burning quality. D-2 REPORT The sample shall be deemed to have satisfied the test for burning quality if all the bidis tested burn continuouslv for 80 percent of their lengths. �

ANNEX E
( Clause 6)
SAMPLING OF BIDIS
E-l GENERAL REQUIREMENTS FOR SAMPLING E-1.1 In drawing, preparing, storing and bandhng samples, the following precautions and directions shall be observed. E-I.2 Precautions shall be taken to draw the samples, so as to protect the samples, the material being sampled and the receptacles for samples from loss or gain of moisture and from adventitious contamination. E-I.3 The samples shall be placed in a clean and dry receptacles. The receptacles for sample shall be sealed air tight after filling and marked with full details of sampling, date of manufacture, name of the manufacturer and other important particulars of the Table 2 Number of bulk Contafaers to be Cbosen for Samplinl

E-l.4 Sample shall be stored in such a manner that the conditions of ..torage do not unduly effect the quality of the material.

E-2.4 These bulk containers shall be chosen at random from the lot and for this purpose random number table (see IS 4905 : 1969) as agreed to between the purchaser and the vendor shall be used. In case such a table is not available, the procedure given in E-2.4.1 shall be adopted. E-2.4.1 Arrange all the bulk containers in the lot, in one order and count them as 1, 2, 3 , up to r, in a systematic manner, where r is equal to the integral part of the value Nln, N being the total number of containers in the lot and n the number of containers to be chosen (see Table 2). Every rth container thus counted Shall be separated until the requisite number of containers is obtained from the lot to give the sample for test. If r comes out to be a fractional number, its value shall be taken as equal to the integral part of it. E-3 PREPARATION OF SAMPLES E-3.1 Individual Samples

E-l.5 The sampling shall be done by a person agreed to between the purchaser and the vendor in the presence of the purchaser ( or his representative) and the vendor (or his representative ).
E-2 SCALE OF SAMPLING E-2.1 Lot All the bulk containers in a single consignment of the material pertaining to the same brand shall constitute a lot. It the consignrnent is declared to consist of different brands the bulk containers belonging to the same brand shall be grouped together to constitute separate lots.

One packet of bidls shall be taken out at random from each selected bulk container so as to give about 500 bldts. Out or these bidis so taken out, 100 bidis shall be first tested tor E-2.2 The samples shall be tested for each lot mass of tabacco contained in them and the for ascertaining conformity of the materials mass of wrapper leaves, 5 for freedom from to the requirements of this specification. mould attack and 5 for freedom from tobacco beetle attack. constitute an individual sample representing the bulk container and shall be transferred immediately to thoroughly clean and dry receptacles and sealed air-tight. The receptacles shall be labelled with the particulars given in E-l.3. 1:-3.1.1 The individual samples so obtained from the lot shall be divided into three sets in such a way that every set has an individual sample representing each selected bulk container. One of these sets shall be marked for the purchaser. another for the vendor and the third for the referee, and all the three sets shall bear the seals of the purchaser and the vendor. E-3.2 Composite Sample Prom the portion of the tobacco left over after preparing the individual sample (see �-3.1 ), equal quantities of tobacco mixture shall be taken for each selected bulk container and mixed together well to form a composite sample of about ISO g for the lot. E-3.2.1 The composite sample shall be divided into three equal parts, one for the purchaser, another for the vendor and the third for the referee, and all the three sets shall bear the seals of the purchaser and the vendor. E-3.3 Referee Sample Referee sample shall consist of a set of individual samples (see E-3.1) and a composite sample ( see E-3.2), marked for this purpose and shall bear the seals of the purchaser and the vendor. These shall be kept at a place agreed to between the two. E-4 NUMBER OF TESTS E-4.1 Tests for the determination of loss on drying and nicotine shall be conducted on each of the individual samples in a set (see E-3.1 ). �.4.2 The tests for the determination of the remaining characteristics shall be conducted on the composite sample ( see E-3.2 ). E-5 CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY to the specification, when: a) each of the test results for loss on heating and nicotine satisfies tbe corresponding requirement specified in Table 1. If, however, one or more test results do not satisfy the corresponding requirement, the conformity of the lot shall be acertained in accordance with E-5.1.1; and
b) The test results on the composite sample for the remaining characteristics satisfy the corresponding requirements specified in Table J.

E-S.I.l In case one or more of the test results do not satisfy the requirements for Joss on heating, and nicotine, the following procedure shall be adopted for determining conformity of the material in respect of these characteristics: The mean (X) and the range (R) of the corresponding test results shall be calculated as: Mean ( X ) Sum of the test results Number of the test results

Range (R) = Difference between the highest and the lowest values obtained for the test results. The appropriate expressions as shown in col 6 of Table 3 shall be calculated. If the values of these expressions satisfy the relevant conditions as given in col 6 of Table 3, the lot shall be deemed to have satisfied the requirements for loss on heating and nicotine.
